record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Determine whether the known bounds for constructing plane spanners that simultaneously have low total weight and bounded maximum degree are tight.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 16. Are these bounds tight?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a finite set of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane. A geometric graph on $P$ is a straight-line graph whose vertex set is $P$, with edge weights equal to the Euclidean lengths of the corresponding segments. A geometric graph $G$ is called a plane $t$-spanner of $P$ (for some real constant $t \geq 1$, called the stretch factor) if (i) no two edges of $G$ cross, and (ii) for every pair of points $p, q \in P$, the length of a shortest path from $p$ to $q$ in $G$ is at most $t \cdot \|pq\|$, where $\|pq\|$ is the Euclidean distance.

The total weight $w(G)$ of $G$ is the sum of its edge weights, and $w(\mathrm{MST}(P))$ denotes the weight of a Euclidean minimum spanning tree of $P$. The maximum degree $\Delta(G)$ is the largest number of edges incident to any vertex.

It is known that for every finite point set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ one can construct, in $O(n \log n)$ time, a plane $t$-spanner $G$ of $P$ satisfying simultaneously
\[
\Delta(G) \leq D, \qquad t \leq T, \qquad w(G) \leq C \cdot w(\mathrm{MST}(P)),
\]
for certain absolute constants $D$, $T$, and $C$ achieved by existing constructions.

Question: Are the currently known constants $D$, $T$, and $C$ for the simultaneous bounded-degree, bounded-stretch, low-weight plane spanner problem tight? More precisely, determine matching lower bounds (or improved upper bounds) on the achievable triples $(D, T, C)$ such that every $n$-point set in the plane admits a plane $t$-spanner with maximum degree at most $D$, stretch factor at most $T$, and total weight at most $C \cdot w(\mathrm{MST}(P))$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., experimental and algorithmic studies through the early 2020s) continues to refine the constants for degree, stretch, and weight in plane spanner constructions, with at least 11 known algorithms offering different tradeoffs. No publication establishes that the simultaneous bounds on degree, stretch factor, and weight-to-MST ratio are tight; the constants in known proofs are widely regarded as worst-case artifacts. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Bounded-Degree Plane Geometric Spanners in Practice
status_evidence.snippet: To date, 11 algorithms have been designed... constants are worst case constants that are artifacts of the proofs, and in practice, they are believed to be much smaller.
status_evidence.claim: Constants in known constructions are not known to be tight; multiple algorithms with different tradeoffs continue to be studied.

status_evidence.title: Lower Bounds on the Dilation of Plane Spanners
status_evidence.snippet: Dumitrescu and Ghosh address lower bounds on the dilation of plane spanners.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bounds on plane spanner stretch factors are an active area, with gaps remaining between known upper and lower bounds.

status_evidence.title: Constructing Plane Spanners of Bounded Degree and Low Weight
status_evidence.snippet: O(n log n)-time algorithm constructs a plane t-spanner with t ≈ 10, degree ≤ 27, weight proportional to MST.
status_evidence.claim: Best known simultaneous bounds for degree, stretch, and weight have specific constants whose tightness is not established.
